text:
Sam (product): Quick sync — first cut of the Dedicated Capacity PRD (SLA + autoscale + burst mechanics) is up. Need a fast sanity check on acceptance criteria and edge behaviors. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/dedicated-capacity-sla :eyes:
Maria (eng): Reading. Quick Q — what do we mean by 'burst credits'? Is that pre-warmed instances or a short-term overcommit queue?
Sam (product): @Maria good call — burst credits = short-lived GPU pool above committed capacity. Consumed as tokens/min, replenishes slowly. Purpose: handle short fanouts without forcing permanent commit. Numbers provisional.
Jon (infra): We need a precise autoscale policy in the doc. Proposal: scale by GPU units. Trigger scale-up when sustained token throughput > 70% capacity for 60s. Scale-down after idle 300s. Add cooldown to avoid flapping.
Li (sre): SLO questions: 99.95% p99 latency target is fine for steady-state, but do we allow an expanded p99 window for cold-cache (KV miss) or pre-warm windows? We should define acceptable degradation and fallback behavior.
Anya (customer success): FYI — FinCo asked that burst be guaranteed up to 3x baseline during business hours and that any failure to meet burst triggers penalty clause. They also want per-minute cost estimates when burst is used.
Sam (product): Draft acceptance criteria I'm proposing:
- Steady-state throughput verified for each commit tier (e.g., tier S = 100k req/min at 512 tokens) with p50/p95/p99 latency targets.
- Burst test: 3x baseline sustained for 30s, error rate < 5%.
- Autoscale: additional GPUs scheduled/ready within 60s of threshold, scale-down cooldown >= 300s, never reduce below min_provisioned.
- Fallback: automatic routing to lower-parameter model or backup region if scale-up fails.
Maria (eng): For CI load test we can add a harness. Example run: 
```bash
./loadtest --rps 20000 --concurrency 256 --payload=512
```
Jon (infra): Example operational config to include in PRD: 
```yaml
autoscale:
  metric: tokens_per_sec
  scale_up_threshold: 70000
  scale_up_window: 60s
  scale_down_window: 300s
  cooldown: 120s
  max_gpus: 50
  min_gpus: 2
```
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: canary=10% traffic -> rollout window=30m -> monitors = [error_rate, tail_latency, deploy_anomaly]. /deploy status
Li (sre): Edge cases to capture in the PRD tests: GPU preemption on shared clouds, KV cache mass-eviction events, transient network blips, and queued requests that cause head-of-line latency. Add regression tests that simulate KV eviction + 2x request burst.
Sam (product): Good list. We'll add acceptance tests for EV (`kv_eviction + burst`) and a fallback policy that routes to a lower-capacity but always-available model variant. Also adding a soft-SLO bucket for cold-cache where p99 can be relaxed to X ms for up to Y minutes during ramp.
Anya (customer success): I'll confirm FinCo contract language for burst guarantees and penalty thresholds. They also want traceable per-request IDs and a simple cost estimate UI for minutes of burst usage.
Maria (eng): I'll stub the load harness and add testcases to CI. Can we get a cost model from finance to estimate $/token during burst vs committed?
Sam (product): Noted — will loop in Finance. Also need a clear rollback plan in PRD: if canary shows >1% error or p99 spike >2x baseline, rollback to previous config and enable fallback.
Jon (infra): Add autoscale safety limits: max scale-up step and global admission control to protect control plane. Also include a scaling hysteresis to prevent oscillation.
Li (sre): For incident playbooks: define runbook for "failed scale-up" and "post-burst capacity exhaustion". Steps: 1) enable fallback routing, 2) notify oncall, 3) escalate to infra. Log samples to capture: `scale_event`, `kv_eviction`, `route_decision`.
Sam (product): I'll incorporate runbook snippets and the test matrix. @Anya can you confirm FinCo and any other enterprise asks by EOD tomorrow?
Anya (customer success): Will do, I'll sync and post notes here by EOD.
Maria (eng): Quick question on measurement: should we use tokens/sec or active_requests as primary autoscale metric? Tokens/sec is better for gen workloads; active_requests can be noisy.
Jon (infra): Use tokens/sec + 95th pct GPU utilisation as a cross-check. Both in the autoscale policy.
Sam (product): Great. I'll update the PRD with these specifics (autoscale YAML, acceptance test steps, runbooks, fallback policy). Pinging for final sign-off tomorrow morning. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
